A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KB-aligned PCA framework for OOD detection. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison despite pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original OOD detection experiments, attack evaluations, human and LLM assessments of RAG responses, latency measurements, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including detection accuracies, response-quality evaluations, latency measurements, and supplementary experiments.

M1.justification: PCA, EVR and p-value component selection, the six lightweight detectors, and the RAG procedure remain unchanged. Section 3 adds explanations of domain-specific fitting and shared projected features without establishing a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same COVID-19, Substance Use, StackExchange, MS MARCO, 4chan, and synthetic-query coverage. The expanded description of the existing 201-sample 4chan evaluation does not introduce a new population or scenario.

E2.justification: Mahalanobis, kNN, ViM, and ODIN remain in the corresponding comparisons. GPT-4o comparator configurations, including the appendix prompt variants and uncertainty-aware method, are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The 90:10 split, balanced classes, initial 200 PCs, embedding models, retrieval settings, evaluation sample sizes, and annotation procedures are retained. Added explanations of KB construction and labeling document existing settings.

E4.justification: The encoder and PC sensitivity studies, alternative generators and judges, prompt optimization, error analyses, and qualitative PC investigations remain unchanged in the appendices. The new synthetic-data caveat introduces no robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same standard-deviation reporting, t-tests, agreement calculations, and five-pass uncertainty-aware GPT-4o procedure. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Section 5.1 revises the reported dimensionality reduction from two orders of magnitude to roughly one to two orders. Table and plotted values are unchanged; Section 5.3's newly stated totals of 182/300 and 215/300 summarize the existing GMM and GPT-4o counts in Table 3.

T1.justification: The projection equations, component-selection rules, geometric definitions, complexity analysis, and appendix agreement formula are retained. Corrections to projected-embedding notation and the dimensionality symbol do not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The conclusion narrows the prompted-LLM comparison from matching strong baselines to being competitive, supported by Section 5.3's explicit qualification concerning OOD recall. The main PCA-based detection and response-relevance contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 explicitly acknowledges GMM's OOD-recall disadvantage and frames deployment as a latency/cost trade-off. The limitations section adds that synthetic queries may separate ID and OOD too cleanly, overstating performance on difficult real-world boundary cases.

D1.justification: Sections 3–4 clarify per-KB fitting, expert answers as KB documents, and answerability-based labeling of the existing 4chan subset. The advertised code location changes from the toastedqu repository to the chateval repository. These are documentation and access-instruction changes.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds Stacey et al. (2026) and positions KB-based abstention as complementary to improving generator OOD generalization. Logistic-regression references replace Kleinbaum et al. with Berkson, Hosmer et al., and McCullagh; several other reference changes update publication metadata.

P1.justification: Targeted expansions explain the two studies, detector inputs, KB/query distinction, and performance trade-offs. Grammar and cross-references are corrected, an affiliation changes, and acknowledgments are added. The overall section structure and most appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains a clarifying caption, some tables are resized or repositioned, and Figure 28 moves from a separate appendix page to below Table 35. The same figures and tables remain, with unchanged graphical content.

improvement.justification: The unchanged Table 3 shows GMM detecting 48/150 OOD queries versus GPT-4o's 89/150. v3 acknowledges this trade-off more clearly, adds a specific synthetic-data limitation, and clarifies KB construction. These changes improve transparency and qualify the conclusions, while the underlying empirical evidence remains unchanged.
